title: The man at the crossing
body: Every morning at seven, a man in a yellow coat stands at the crossing near our school gate. His name is Uncle Fang. He is not a policeman. He is a retired worker who lives in the next street. He started six winters ago, after a small accident happened at the same corner. Nobody asked him to do it. He knows the children who cross there every day. He knows who walks fast and who dreams while walking. "Slow down, little runner," he says. On rainy days he brings a big umbrella. The parents who wait on the other side often bring him hot water. Last term our class wrote him a card. He read it twice, then put it in his coat pocket. He is a gentle man whom nobody in our school forgets.

options: A policeman at the school gate.
A teacher from our school.
A retired worker who lives in the next street.
A parent who waits for his child.
questions.explanation: 'He is not a policeman. He is a retired worker who lives in the next street.'

questions.q: Why did Uncle Fang start his work?
options: Because a small accident happened at the corner.
Because the school paid him.
Because the police asked him to help.
Because he wanted to meet the parents.
questions.explanation: 'He started six winters ago, after a small accident happened at the same corner. Nobody asked him to do it.'

questions.q: How do people show their thanks to him?
options: They give him a yellow coat.
They walk him home after school.
They ask the school to pay him.
They bring him hot water and write him cards.
questions.explanation: 'The parents who wait on the other side often bring him hot water.' 与 'Last term our class wrote him a card.'

title: The last bus
body: The last bus of the night leaves the station at half past eleven. Driver Song has taken this line for nine years. Most of the people who get on after eleven are tired. Some workers fall asleep before the third stop. Driver Song drives slowly at that hour. When he comes to a sleeping passenger's stop, he says the name of the street twice, in a low voice. One winter night a young woman missed her stop because she was crying. He did not ask why. He drove to the end of the line, then took her back for free. "Everyone has a bad night," he once told a neighbour. He is a quiet man whom his passengers seldom thank. But the workers who ride the last bus all know his voice.

questions.q: What is special about the way Driver Song drives at night?
options: He drives faster to save time.
He drives slowly and calls out the stops in a low voice.
He stops the bus at every corner.
He asks the passengers to stay awake.
questions.explanation: 'Driver Song drives slowly at that hour. When he comes to a sleeping passenger's stop, he says the name of the street twice, in a low voice.'

questions.q: What did he do for the young woman?
options: He asked her why she was crying.
He called her family.
He gave her some money.
He took her back to her stop for free.
questions.explanation: 'He drove to the end of the line, then took her back for free.'

questions.q: What does the last sentence tell us?
options: The night workers know him well even if they seldom say thanks.
The passengers often write to the bus company.
He wants to change to a daytime line.
His voice is too low for passengers to hear.
questions.explanation: 'He is a quiet man whom his passengers seldom thank. But the workers who ride the last bus all know his voice.'

title: She knows every name
body: Aunt Mei cleans the third floor of our teaching building. She starts at six and finishes at four. She is the only person in the building who knows every student by name. Nobody taught her. She just listens. When a boy loses his key, he goes to her first. When a girl feels ill in the afternoon, she sits in the small room beside the stairs, and Aunt Mei brings her warm water. Last year countless leaves fell into the corridor after a storm. Six students who live near the school came back on Sunday to help her. They finished before lunch. "You did not have to come," she said. "Neither did you," one boy answered.

questions.q: What is special about Aunt Mei?
options: She starts work later than the teachers.
She teaches students in the small room.
She knows every student in the building by name.
She lives near the school gate.
questions.explanation: 'She is the only person in the building who knows every student by name.'

questions.q: What happens when a student feels ill in the afternoon?
options: Aunt Mei brings her warm water.
Aunt Mei calls her parents.
Aunt Mei takes her home.
Aunt Mei asks a teacher for help.
questions.explanation: 'When a girl feels ill in the afternoon, she sits in the small room beside the stairs, and Aunt Mei brings her warm water.'

questions.q: What does the boy's answer mean?
options: He was sorry that he came so late.
Aunt Mei helps them without having to, so they help her the same way.
He wanted Aunt Mei to thank them.
He thought the work was too hard.
questions.explanation: '"You did not have to come," she said. "Neither did you," one boy answered.' 意为她平日的帮助同样不是分内之事。

title: The river team
body: In our town there is a small team of about twenty people. They are not soldiers. They are shop owners, drivers and teachers who go to the river when someone is in danger. The leader is a woman who runs a noodle shop near the bridge. Her phone never turns off. In summer the water rises quickly. The team members who live close to the bridge get there first. They carry ropes, not cameras. Two years ago they helped a survivor of a boat accident. He came back last spring with his family and ate at the noodle shop. He did not say much. He just washed the bowls before he left. The leader kept his photo behind the door. "He is one of us now," she says.

questions.q: Who are the members of the river team?
options: Soldiers from a nearby town.
Students from the local school.
Doctors and nurses.
Shop owners, drivers and teachers.
questions.explanation: 'They are shop owners, drivers and teachers who go to the river when someone is in danger.'

questions.q: Why do the members who live close to the bridge get there first?
options: Because they have the best boats.
Because they live nearest to the river.
Because they are the youngest.
Because the leader calls them first.
questions.explanation: 'The team members who live close to the bridge get there first.'

questions.q: What did the survivor do when he came back?
options: He washed the bowls in the noodle shop.
He gave the team new ropes.
He joined the team at once.
He took a photo with the leader.
questions.explanation: 'He did not say much. He just washed the bowls before he left.'
